test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held On: 30 June, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The executive power of the Union in India rests with _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per the Indian Constitution**, the **executive authority of the Union** is vested in the **President,** who may exercise it directly or through subordinate officers.
 
• However, the practical exercise of executive power is primarily conducted by the **Council of Ministers,** under the leadership of the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister, a member of **either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha**, must meet certain eligibility criteria.
 
• They must be **at least 25 years old if they are a Lok Sabha member, or at least 30 years **old if they are a Rajya Sabha member.
 
• Additionally, they must be a citizen of India and cannot hold any profit-making office under the Indian government.
 
• While there is no term limit for the Prime Minister, they must maintain the confidence of both the President and the Lok Sabha to remain in office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The President of India **is elected by an electoral college composed of elected members from both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of the states.
 
• This election is conducted through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote method.
 
• To ensure fairness and equity, each vote is given suitable weightage to maintain uniformity among states and parity between the states and the Union.
 
• The President must fulfill certain eligibility criteria, including being a citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, and qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Their term of office spans five years, and they are eligible for re-election. Removal from office follows the procedure outlined in Article 61 of the Constitution.
